claim: Let \(k\) be a field of characteristic \(p>0\), let \(n\ge 2\), and let \(\mathrm{PGL}_n(k)\) act on \(\mathbb P^{n-1}(k)\) through entrywise Frobenius \(F([A])=[A^{(p)}]\). For \(x=[x_1:\cdots:x_n]\), set \(V_x=\operatorname{span}_{k^p}\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\subset k\). Then two points lie in the same orbit exactly when \(V_y=cV_x\) for some \(c\in k^\times\); hence the orbit set is in bijection with homothety classes of nonzero finite-dimensional \(k^p\)-subspaces \(V\subset k\) of dimension at most \(n\). In particular, the action is transitive if and only if \(k\) is perfect.

correctness.rationale: For every point, the coordinate-span homothety class is invariant under projective matrices over \(k^p\). Conversely, after rescaling representatives to give the same span \(V\), the two surjections \((k^p)^n\to V\) differ by a domain automorphism, yielding a projective matrix over \(k^p\) between the points. Every permitted \(V\) is realized by choosing a basis as homogeneous coordinates. Perfectness gives one class; imperfectness gives distinct classes of dimensions one and two.
